name: THE RAIL YARD'S SHOPS
rule: VAMILY rules 416 (the big interiors: the tile stays a house), 461 (more boards), 451(a) (its ceiling at 10%), 59 (every tile its cost and its effect), 428, 441.
facts: A rail yard's locomotive shop is a long shed with tracks running through it, engines over inspection pits, work platforms at cab height along them, the parts and wheel sets stacked on the floor; its freight house is a long dock of boxcars and crates.
A road locomotive is about 22 metres long and nearly five high; a boxcar about 15 metres.
On house tiles a locomotive is a run of tiles nobody stands on and nobody sees through; the rails across the floor are ground a man steps over, slowly.
how_to_mod: A layout is 15 strings of 20 characters; every character is in 'legend'; every tile kind a legend entry names has its row in 'tiles' (its cost and its effect). A piece names the finished piece it is drawn as ('like') until this folder has its own art file (railshop_art.json: floor lists and a kit, the garage's format). slices/bohemia_big_inside.js lays it; slices/fight_ground/insides.json lists the insides.
districts_why: The rail yard is mostly track under the sky: about one fight in three there is fought inside its engine shop or its freight house, by the cell's own dice; the rest among the cars and the rails outside.
tiles_how: Rule 59: every kind of tile says what it costs to step on and what it does. 'row' is the fight's own ground row (flat 2 AP, rough 3, height +1 a level, obstacles none); 'open' is open floor (on AUTO nobody stays on it); 'good' is ground AUTO goes to; 'say' is the one line he reads when he taps it (draft, the fewest words); 'sight' says whether a blocker hides a man ('blocked', the obstacles row) or is seen past ('seen'). [bb] each kind is a Battle Brothers ground: flat, rough, an obstacle, and cover as its trees and walls give it.

wall.effect: The shop's brick wall: no way through, no sight through.

floor.effect: The shop's oil-black floor: open ground, nothing to hide behind; on AUTO nobody stays on it.

rails.effect: A track across the floor, its rails and ties: no cover, and slow going over them (3 AP). [bb] its rough ground.

loco.effect: A locomotive over its pit, nearly five metres high: nobody stands there, and nobody sees through it; cover beside it. [bb] its wall.

platform.effect: A work platform at cab height on its legs, open underneath: nobody stands on it on house tiles; seen past; cover beside it. [bb] its palisade you see through.

boxcar.effect: A boxcar at the dock, its door rolled back: nobody stands there, and nobody sees through it; cover beside it. [bb] its wall.

wheels.effect: Wheel sets on their axles, stacked: cover.

toolchest.effect: A rolling tool chest: low cover.

parts.effect: A traction motor and parts on a skid: cover.

racks.effect: Parts racks against the wall, floor to beam: nobody stands there, and nobody sees through them. [bb] its wall.

crates.effect: Freight crates left on the dock: cover.

cart.effect: A baggage cart, its tongue down: low cover.

cages.effect: The freight house's cages for small parcels, mesh: nobody passes; you see through it; cover beside it. [bb] its palisade you see through.

fire.effect: A fire somebody keeps in a drum. It burns day and night: a man in its light is seen.
fire.say_lit: A fire: you stand in its light, and they see you.

doors.effect: The shop's big doors where the track comes in, open: open ground, and by day the light falls in: a man here is seen.
doors.say_lit: The doors: open ground, and the day is on you.

kit_how: Every piece is drawn AS a finished piece of another kit ('like') until COOK's own picture for it is in railshop_art.json under the same name: then that picture is used and nothing here changes. 'kind' is what it does in the fight (COVER, LOW_COVER, WALL); 'blocks_move' means nobody stands on its tile.
start_why: NO HIGH GROUND: the work platforms stand at cab height, but on house tiles they are a thing to go round, not a storey.

ceiling.how: VAMILY rule 451(a): the shop's roof trusses, its smoke jacks and the overhead crane's rail, over the board at this alpha. 'src' is the picture COOK makes; 'have' true the day it is in the folder. Until then the fight draws 'kind' itself, a stand-in (the warehouse's roof).
